description: Shared block-device topology contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server (agent issue #155). Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/io_topology_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_io.py::test_contract_fixture_round_trip -- each scenario's 'sysfs' is materialized as a real directory tree (whole devices as /sys/block/<name> symlinks, partitions as subdirectories carrying a `partition` file, slaves/ and multipath/ as symlinks, `device` as a symlink, `hidden` and `wwid` as attribute files) and io_topology() must equal scenario['payload']['io_topology']. The server ingests data['io_topology'] == payload['io_topology'] BESIDE data['io'] from the same tick; it is a separate, top-level config flag (config['io_topology'] = true, a plain boolean). 'sysfs' is an agent-side input the server ignores. Change the payload shape only in lockstep with the server spec and its byte-identical fixture copy.
_agent_min_version_note: MINOR on the 1.x train: a new collector. Gate the config flag on it (older agents ignore the unknown key, so an ungated flag is harmless, just inert).
null_contract: data['io_topology'] ABSENT (an older agent, or the flag off), null (a non-Linux host, /sys/block could not be listed, or the sysfs read stalled past the agent's 5s bound -- then null on every tick until that read returns) and {} (no entry could be read or placed) all mean NOT REPORTED: the server keeps its current name rules for every io row. None of them means 'no stacking'.
entry_contract: Keys are device names spelled exactly as the `io` rows spell them (/proc/diskstats names). sysfs writes '/' as '!' (cciss!c0d0), but a '!' can also be literal (md takes any md_* array name verbatim), so the agent escapes each /proc/diskstats name the way the kernel does ('/' -> '!') and looks the sysfs name up by that: cciss!c0d0 is reported as 'cciss/c0d0', md_data! stays 'md_data!', md_a!b! is 'md_a/b!'. A name no diskstats name escapes to (or one two of them escape to) is left out, along with any layer that lists it as a slave. Every entry has exactly one of two shapes. WHOLE DEVICE: {'slaves': [names], 'virtual': bool} -- slaves are the devices it is stacked on, read from /sys/block/<dev>/slaves/ plus, for an NVMe native-multipath head, its hidden per-path disks (from /sys/block/<dev>/multipath/ on Linux 6.15+, else each hidden disk matched to the one visible disk sharing its wwid) -- sorted; they may be partitions such as 'sda1' or other layers such as 'md0', and need not appear in `io`; [] means nothing beneath it, and is only ever reported from a successful read. virtual is true when the device has no `device` link, i.e. its driver registered it with no parent device (md, dm, bcache, drbd, loop, brd/ram, zram, nbd, zvol). It describes the driver model, not the hardware: a paravirtual disk (virtio vda, Xen xvda) is NOT virtual, and neither is Ceph RBD (rbd*), whose parent is its rbd bus device. PARTITION: {'partition_of': '<whole device>'} -- decided structurally (a directory nested in its disk's sysfs entry), never by name. A device that appears in `io` with NO entry is UNKNOWN for that row only (its sysfs entry could not be read, its name could not be placed, or it was removed mid-read): fall back to the name rules for it, do not treat it as a leaf. UNTRUSTED STRINGS: every key, every slaves[] element and every partition_of value is a host-controlled device name (local root can name an md array almost anything); run all three through the same name gate as the `io` keys, and escape them before building any PromQL matcher.
counting_contract: Compute each device's RATE from its own counters first and classify after: a device's class can change between ticks (an entry left out for one tick falls back to name rules, a stalled read makes the whole map null, a multipath head that loses its last path becomes a leaf), so summing raw cumulative counters over the counted set and then differencing would spike by a device's lifetime bytes on every change. To sum host I/O without counting one write at every layer: count whole devices with slaves == [] and virtual == false (the bottom of this host's stack). That total is PHYSICAL DEVICE TRAFFIC, not unique application writes: a RAID1 write is counted twice because two disks really take it, and a bcache write-back lands on both the cache and the backing device. It is the figure the server's current mdraid workaround already reports (array dropped, members kept). Logical I/O -- the tops of the stacks -- is a different figure, and this map does NOT fully support it: it has edges for md, dm (LVM, LUKS, multipath), bcache and partitions, but none from a zvol to its pool's vdevs, from a loop device to the disk holding its file, or from an RBD image to the OSDs, so summing the tops would count those twice. A device with non-empty slaves is a LAYER whose I/O is already counted on the devices it names. A partition's I/O is already counted on partition_of. A virtual device with no slaves (zd*, loop*, zram*, ram*, nbd*) sits on something the kernel does not model as a block device -- a ZFS pool whose vdevs are already counted, a file, RAM, the network -- so it is not physical I/O either; that is the structural form of today's zd/loop/ram/zram noise rule. EXCEPTION, and the one leaf this predicate cannot place: Ceph RBD (rbd*) reads slaves == [] and virtual == false, so it IS counted, although its I/O is network traffic to the Ceph cluster -- and on a hyperconverged host whose OSDs are local disks, the same write is recorded again at those disks, which slaves/ does not express. If RBD must be excluded, that stays a name rule (see scenario 'ceph_rbd_client'). The same holds for iSCSI and NVMe-oF disks: remote storage with a device link, counted as this host's I/O. FALLBACK: if the predicate selects NO whole device while `io` has rows, the host's storage bottoms out in a virtual leaf -- an OpenVZ/Virtuozzo container sees only its ploop device, a diskless host boots from nbd -- and a zero total would be wrong: use today's name rules for that tick (scenario 'openvz_ploop_container'). NVMe native multipath: the head (nvme0n1) and its hidden path disks (nvme0c0n1, ...) are all in /proc/diskstats with the same I/O, and the head lists its paths as slaves, so it is a layer like a dm-multipath map and the paths are the counted leaves (scenario 'nvme_native_multipath'). Before Linux 6.15 there are no multipath/ links; the head is then found by wwid instead (scenario 'nvme_native_multipath_before_6_15'), so the payload is the same. Single-controller NVMe has no head and is a plain leaf. KNOWN GAP: a kernel without the `hidden` block attribute (5.10 and later have it), or a wwid shared by two visible disks, attaches nothing -- the head then reads as a leaf beside its paths, as today's name rules already count it.

mdraid_luks_lvm.description: RAID1 boot + RAID1 data under LUKS under LVM, the classic double-count: one write lands on dm-1, dm-0, md1 and both members. Only sda and sdb are counted; loop0 (a snap) is virtual with no slaves.

zfs_hypervisor.description: Proxmox on ZFS: the pool's vdevs are NVMe partitions, every VM disk is a zvol (virtual, no slaves) with its own partition table, and an md0p1 is a kernel partition of an md array. Only nvme0n1 and nvme1n1 are counted.

bcache_and_multipath.description: bcache0 caches sdd on an NVMe partition, and BOTH appear in its slaves/: the backing device is linked on register (drivers/md/bcache/super.c, bd_link_disk_holder(dc->bdev, ...)) and the cache device when the bcache device attaches to its cache set (bcache_device_link(), bd_link_disk_holder(ca->bdev, ...)); a bcache device with no cache set attached lists only its backing device. dm-0 is a multipath map over two paths (sdb, sdc) to one LUN. Neither layer is visible by name. Counted: nvme0n1, sdb, sdc, sdd -- each I/O takes one path, so the two paths do not double-count each other.

nvme_native_multipath.description: Linux 6.15+: a dual-ported NVMe namespace under native multipath. The head nvme0n1 links its two hidden path disks from multipath/ (not slaves/), and all three rows carry the same I/O in /proc/diskstats. The head reads as a layer over its paths, so only the two paths are counted -- each I/O takes one path. The head's partition belongs to the head.

nvme_native_multipath_before_6_15.description: The same topology on a kernel older than 6.15 (Ubuntu 24.04's 6.8, Debian 13 / RHEL 10's 6.12): no multipath/ links. The path disks are hidden (`hidden` reads 1) and report the head's wwid, so each is matched to the one visible disk with that wwid -- the payload is the same as with the links. nvme1n1 is a single-controller NVMe: no head, not hidden, a plain leaf.

xen_pv_whole_disk_named_like_a_partition.description: A Xen PV guest attached as xvda1/xvda2 with no xvda: both are WHOLE devices (top-level /sys/block entries with a device link), whatever the names suggest. Both are counted.

ceph_rbd_client.description: A Proxmox/Ceph client mapping two RBD images: rbd0/rbd1 have a device link (their parent is the rbd bus device), so they read virtual: false with no slaves, exactly like the local disk. rbd0p1 is a kernel partition of rbd0. By the counting predicate all three whole devices are counted; see counting_contract for why rbd is the exception a structural signal cannot place.

openvz_ploop_container.description: An OpenVZ/Virtuozzo container: its only disk is a ploop device, which the kernel builds itself (no device link, no slaves), with one partition. The counting predicate selects nothing here, so the server must apply counting_contract's FALLBACK (today's name rules), never report a zero total.

device_unreadable.description: dm-0's slaves/ could not be read (here: the device was torn down between the /sys/block listing and the read). It is left OUT -- never reported as a slaves: [] leaf -- so the server falls back to its name rules for that one row. Its neighbours are unaffected.

collection_failure.description: /sys/block could not be listed. null: not reported, the same as an absent key.
